correctness.rationale: For every antiparallel bond, subtracting the two Hamiltonians gives ΔH=2J b(a−d)+4h(−1)^i b; 0<h<J makes the three bond-energy signs decisive. The resulting parity-dependent four-site exclusion rule is necessary and sufficient. Every labeled cyclic word corresponds bijectively to one closed walk in the alternating three-spin transfer graph, weighted once per up-spin. Exact multiplication yields the characteristic factor x^5−(1+z²)x^4−(z+z²+z³)x³−z^5; the logarithmic determinant identity gives the full finite-volume generating function. At z=1 the root-modulus argument proves a unique strictly dominant positive root, so the entropy statement follows for all even sizes. At h=0 neutral swaps are allowed and the no-isolated-spin transfer has dominant root φ. The embedded standalone exact checker validates the determinant, rational series and complete enumerated polynomials for rings of lengths 4–12 at two rational fields; finite tests are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The closest exact published result is De Smedt–Godrèche–Luck (2002), which gives zero-field Kawasaki blocked configurations for both constrained and unconstrained constant-energy exchanges, but not a parity-dependent staggered-site term. Gómez Albarracín–Rosales–Grynberg (2016) derive several proliferation rates for spatially uniform first- and second-neighbor couplings, without the site-alternating energy preference. The new local allowed-word sets differ from all those cases, and their general statements do not imply the displayed quintic generating series. Targeted searches of corresponding terminology and exact polynomial did not identify matching prior coverage. Other equivalent presentations in lattice-gas language remain possible; absolute uniqueness is not asserted.
residual_risks: A hard-to-index publication on binary-periodic lattice-gas site energies or parity-biased Kawasaki exchange might supply the same polynomial or a general theorem implying it.
The 1991 Cornell–Kaski–Stinchcombe paper was checked at abstract level only; no conclusion about its entire contents follows from that limited access.
As with any bounded literature search, lack of a matching result is not an absolute novelty proof.

value.rationale: A spatially alternating weak field is a natural kinetic perturbation of ferromagnetic Kawasaki exchange because it makes originally neutral spin diffusion energetically directional without altering the strong ferromagnetic condensation moves. The result classifies all absorbing states, resolves every magnetization sector via an exact bivariate rational generating function, and shows a discontinuous, nonzero shift of the thermodynamic absorbing-state entropy for any positive weak field. This is a structural infinite-family phase-space change, not a finite-size table, a variable renaming, or a claim about dynamic selection probabilities.
